note: The answerability fixture (ADR-1009 / LEG-I). Each row is a real situation a reader arrives
with, and the clause ids that must be PRESENT on the named rendered page for that situation
to have an answer. An unanswered row is a completeness FAILURE -- the finding class that
fails for insufficiency rather than for rule-breaking, which is the thing arc-design-cycle3
2026-07-30 said a quality gate must have and did not.
Committed in its own commit BEFORE the lint that reads it exists, per ADR-1009: a pass
condition written after the numbers are visible is chosen to flatter (arc-absorb 2026-08-10).
`answered_by` is ALL-of, not any-of. A row listing two clauses is asserting that neither one
alone answers the question, and a page carrying only one of them has half an answer -- which
reads to a lint as a pass and to a reader as a dead end.
`when` is the same single-equality guard vocabulary the templates use, evaluated by the same
`conditionVerdict`. A row whose guard does not hold is NOT APPLICABLE to that venture and is
not counted against it. A row whose guard is MALFORMED is a failure, never a skip: a typo
that silently disables a mandatory check is the exact defect the decision-logic attacker
found in the clause path (fixed-defect-list row 11), and it is not being re-introduced here.
The refund rows name both sides of the window in one question on purpose. A clause that
states a boundary answers day N and day N+1 together; a clause that gestures at
`a reasonable period` answers neither, and splitting that into two rows would let a vague
clause score two passes instead of one failure.
